identity.title: ControlFusion: A Controllable Image Fusion Network with Language-Vision Degradation Prompts

problem.claim: Image fusion under real-world composite degradations must also accommodate user-specific visual preferences.

gap.claim: Existing image fusion methods are described as lacking flexibility for composite degradations and user-specific needs.

contributions.claim: ControlFusion uses language-vision degradation prompts to adaptively mitigate composite degradations.
A physics-based degraded imaging model simulates composite degradations using mechanisms including Retinex theory and atmospheric scattering.
The system combines prompt-modulated restoration and fusion, text-encoded user preferences, and a spatial-frequency visual adapter that perceives degradation from source images.

stated_novelty.claim: The proposed distinction is jointly controlling fusion through user-defined language prompts while supplementing them with source-image degradation perception.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments show ControlFusion outperforming state-of-the-art fusion methods in fusion quality and degradation handling, particularly for real-world and compound degradations.

narrative_sequence.summary: The abstract identifies composite real-world degradations and inflexible user control as limitations of current fusion methods.
It introduces ControlFusion, guided by language-vision degradation prompts.
The approach builds a physics-based degradation simulator and a prompt-modulated restoration-fusion network, with text prompts encoding user-defined degradation types and levels.
A spatial-frequency adapter infers degradation from source images, and the authors report gains over state-of-the-art methods, especially under real-world and compound degradations.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs explicit user prompts with an image-driven adapter intended to reduce complete reliance on user instructions.

lessons.interpretation: Combining controllable inputs with automatic perception can address both preference specification and incomplete or inaccurate instructions.
lessons.application: For a controllable vision system, add an observation-based fallback or correction module alongside user controls, and state clearly how the two information sources interact.
lessons.exception: This pattern may be unsuitable when automatic inference is unreliable or when user control must remain strictly authoritative.

unknowns: No quantitative metrics, datasets, baselines, ablations, or experimental conditions are provided for the reported superiority.
The abstract does not specify how user prompts and automatically perceived degradations are reconciled when they disagree.
